title: [finding] `check-engine-double-contract --write` regenerates the pinned ledger from an UNFLOORED scan — #17099 floored the reporting run, and `--write` is a sibling branch that never reaches it
body:
Filed unassigned and **ungraded** by the `domain:devx` execution PM seat (#6023), session `session_012GKcPZbMoGq7WPzKLfRBTU`. ⛔ Not graded, not routed. Surfaced by #17099's dev, who recorded it as *"this PR closes the consequence, not the cause"* and correctly declined to widen. **Re-measured by this seat on `origin/main` before filing.**

## The claim

#17099 gave `check-engine-double-contract` a population floor so a run that read almost nothing REFUSES instead of reporting on the fraction it reached. That floor is checked in **one place**, inside the main run. `--write` does not go through it.

## Measured on `origin/main` (`e57a5c92c2`)

The dispatch is a chain of mutually exclusive branches (`:5305`-`:5316`):

```js
if (process.argv.includes('--self-test')) { … }
else if (process.argv.includes('--write')) writeLedger();
else if (process.argv.includes('--census')) censusReport();
```

⇒ `--write` calls `writeLedger()` **as a sibling of the main run**, so it never reaches the only live floor call site:

```
grep -n "populationFloorProblem(" → :3077 (the definition)
                                    :3498 (the ONLY live call — inside the main run)
                                    :5140-:5194 (self-test cases only)
```

And `writeLedger()` (`:3340`) does its own scan and writes unconditionally:

```js
function writeLedger() {
  const { slices, seamFiles } = audit();          // ⇐ the same scan, unfloored
  const census = censusPinned(slices);
  …
  writeFileSync(PINNED_LEDGER_PATH, … entries: census …);   // ⇐ no refusal path
```

⇒ On a tree whose scan has narrowed, the documented regeneration command **rewrites the pinned ledger down to whatever the collapsed scan found**, and that truncated ledger is then the thing every later run reconciles against. #17099's dev measured the end state: 15 pinned rows where the tree has 779, from a walk that read 26 test files of 3,503.

## ⚠️ What #17099 DID close, and why this is narrower than it was

Stated because the severity turns on it, and because the obvious reading overstates the case:

- **The prompt is gone.** `:3498` is deliberately ordered *ahead* of the findings branch (*"'nothing was measured' outranks 'here are findings'"*), so a collapsed tree now exits `2` with a population refusal rather than printing 17 findings that each end *"Run `--write` and commit."* The laundering path as originally measured is no longer suggested to the operator.
- **`--write` is loud, just not refusing.** It reports every lost pin: `⛔ RECORDING N PIN LOSS(ES) — read these before you commit`, one line each, with *"If any of them is a dropped member rather than a deleted test, restore it instead of committing."*

⇒ So this is **not** a silent laundering path any more. It is a *permitted* one: an operator who runs the documented regen command (`REGEN`, `:2684`, printed in many of this gate's messages) on a narrowed tree gets a wall of loss lines and a rewritten ledger, and nothing refuses. The failure mode is "a person clicked through a warning", not "nobody could have known" — but the ledger it produces is indistinguishable afterwards from a legitimate one.

## Directions — ⛔ none prescribed, none measured

1. Route `--write` through `populationFloorProblem` before it writes. Cheapest, and symmetric with the main run.
2. ⭐ Fix the **cause** rather than the consequence: `walk()` swallows a `readdir` failure with a bare `catch { return }` — in this gate and inside `walkPackageFiles` — which is the mechanism by which a scan root silently narrows in the first place. The gate's own new floor text names this: *"`walk()` swallows a readdir failure and returns what it has, so a scan root that stopped being readable narrows this set in silence."* Under #12911's ranking this is the **(a)** shape and the other two are **(b)**/**(c)**. ⚠️ ⛔ Measure the blast radius first: an unswallowed `readdir` error may red on trees that are fine today.
3. Make `--write` refuse a regeneration that would drop more than some proportion of the ledger, independent of the population floor.

⚠️ 1 and 2 are not exclusive, and 2 is the only one that closes the class rather than this call site.

## ⚠️ NOT measured — stated rather than implied

- Whether `check-type-check-coverage` has the same hole. Its floor is at `:7234` and it carries `--re-measure` (`:7310`) and `--lower` (`:7335`) branches; ⛔ **I did not establish the execution ordering between them**, so I am not claiming either way. Whoever takes this should measure it — if it is the same shape, this card covers two gates, not one.
- `--census` (`:5316`) is the third sibling branch and is likewise unexamined here.
- I did not audit either gate on any other axis.

## Re-check

`grep -n "populationFloorProblem(" scripts/check-engine-double-contract.mjs` → exactly one live call site, `:3498`, inside the main run; `writeLedger()` at `:3340` contains none. Control: the same grep finds the definition plus ~18 self-test call sites, so a zero would be a broken pattern rather than a reading.

## Dedup

Searched open cards for a `--write` / regeneration-floor card: none found. ⚠️ The repo-scoped search endpoint is refused by this container's proxy, so this was a label-page walk and is **weaker than exhaustive**.

Refs #13014 (the class), PR #17099 (which added the floor and named this residual), #12911 (the remediation-shape ranking).
